newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi paper assails Turkey over U.S. flights.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi paper assails Turkey over U.S. flights.

text.p: An official Iraqi newspaper condemned Turkey on Thursday for allowing the United States and Britain to extend their use of its airbases to patrol the skies of northern Iraq.
"The Turkish decision is not independent and nationalist... It smells of a conspiracy against Iraq," said al-Thawra, organ of the ruling Baath party.

Turkish MPs voted on Wednesday to give Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's government the power to authorise continued flights over northern Iraq after the mandate for the current operation, known as Provide Comfort, expires on December 31.
U.S., French and British planes have been shielding Iraq's Kurds from Baghdad since hundreds of thousands of Kurds fled to Turkey and Iran after a failed uprising at the end of the 1991 Gulf War.
Thawra said Turkey adopted the decision as a result of "American and British threats and pressure. Even bribes were given in order to influence the Turkish policy."
A Turkish foreign minister official said on Wednesday that France had decided to withdraw its support for the force.

"Turkey should have taken an independent decision like that of France...France took part in setting up the so-called 'Hammer Force' (in 1991) and participated in its activities but it is no more convinced of its tasks," the Iraqi newspaper said.
In Washington, the White House said it was confident that France would soon rejoin the operation.
Last week the Iraqi ruling party's newspaper warned Ankara that bilateral ties would be damaged if Turkey extended the operation which uses Incirlik in south Turkey as its airbase.

Turkey has been a major outlet for Iraqi oil to world markets since Iraq resumed limited exports via pipeline under an oil-for-food deal with the United Nations this month. Iraq was barred from exporting oil under U.N. sanctions imposed for its invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
